text:
Alex C.: quick sync — want to reconcile warmup credit topology with the policy quirks we hit in staging yesterday
Sara N.: yep, saw the spike. summary: a tenant requested burst, scaled instances started, but warmup credits couldn't be applied because of topology mismatch :grimacing:
Matt P.: +1. the short version: credits are tracked per-pool-shard but the new topology splits shards by topology-id, so credits ended up against a different shard than the admission path used
Joan L.: hmm. is this the same failure where the autoscaler prewarm job created nodes in the wrong AZ and admission rejected them due to tenant-affinity?
Sara N.: related. prewarm created nodes in az-b while the admission flow expected az-a for that tenant (due to stale placement metadata). credits were consumed but not visible to the admission check
Alex C.: can we list the concrete options? I'm thinking:
1) Make credits globally visible to all shards in a pool (simple for admission but larger blast radius)
2) Keep per-shard credits but add a reconciliation / transfer step on prewarm completion
3) Change admission to allow honoring credits attached to sibling shards when topology differs
Matt P.: option 1 is simplest for correctness, but then a buggy tenant could accidentally consume credits across the entire pool — defeats isolation guarantees
Joan L.: option 2 seems safest but adds complexity: we need a reliable transfer protocol and correctness under partial failure. what happens if transfer fails mid-rollout?
Ryan G.: transfer can be implemented via idempotent ledger ops: mark prewarm intent -> acquire temporary credit -> attach to node -> on success, commit transfer; on failure, refund. still worry about edge cases during operator restarts
Sara N.: option 3 is interesting: change admission to look for credits in "nearby" shards with same pool and compatible topology. we'd need an ordering and a TTL to avoid double-spend
Matt P.: double-spend is the major risk. if admission is parallelized, two admissions could both read the same sibling credit and use it concurrently
Alex C.: what about using a leasing primitive: admission grabs a short-lived lease on a credit record before consuming tokens. lease ensures another concurrent admission can't claim the same credit until lease expiry or commit
Joan L.: that sounds plausible. requirements:
- leases must be cheap and distributed
- lease acquisition latency must be < admission budget (we target 20ms additional)
- recovery path: if lease-holder dies, tokens should revert after TTL
Ryan G.: can we piggyback on existing reservation tokens? we already have a reservation token RPC used for warmup; extend it to include a `lease_id` and `sibling_search` flag
Matt P.: RPC extension is low-risk. but the backend store is the question: current ledger is a Dynamo-like store with 50ms p99. that'll blow our admission budget unless we cache leases locally and reconcile lazily
Sara N.: caching leases locally then reconciling with the ledger could work: admission fast-path -> local lease check -> attempt remote commit async. fall back to slower path if remote commit fails
Alex C.: risks: race on cache invalidation; more complexity in failure modes; also cost of remote commits at scale. tradeoff: complexity vs guaranteed isolation
Joan L.: another angle: relax isolation constraints for warmup credits only. treat them as optimistic prewarm hints; if mismatch occurs, worst-case tenant is denied burst for a short time. that keeps system simpler
Ryan G.: but customers expect prewarm to be reliable. if we degrade reliability even rarely, support pages will light up
Matt P.: we could make it a feature flag: optimistic sibling-lookup enabled for low-tier tenants where cost isolation less critical; strict mode for enterprise with hard isolation and reconciliation
Sara N.: feature flag + metrics + automated rollback on error spike sounds pragmatic. rollout plan:
- proto: implement sibling lookup + local lease cache behind feature flag
- test: soak in staging for 48h with synthetic spikes
- rollout: enable for 10% of traffic, monitor double-spend / admission latencies
- if errors < threshold, increase to 100% or flip for specific orgs
Alex C.: agree. add audit trail: every credit use should record origin shard and resolved shard in the event log for forensic debugging
Joan L.: can we also add a periodic consistency job that scans ledgers and reconciles credits across shards? helps when transfers partially fail
Ryan G.: yes — run reconciliation as low-priority background job. it'll produce metrics we can alert on (credit drift, unresolved transfers)
Matt P.: small implementation note: proto schema for the ledger should be backwards compatible. add `resolved_shard` and `lease_id` fields optional
Sara N.: I'll draft a short RFC addendum with diagrams and a canary plan. tagging @Ryan G. for the lease semantics section and @Matt P. for backend performance mitigations
Alex C.: thanks. one more: let's add a chaosplan for prewarm failure modes (node created in wrong az, transfer fail, network partition). ensure automatic refund path is covered by SRE runbook
autoscaler-bot: [scale-event] prewarm: tenant=acme-corp request=8gpus intent=warmup job_id=prewarm-1718001109 status=created
Ryan G.: noted, I'll add runbook snippets and fallout tickets for cross-AZ prewarm constraints
Matt P.: ack. I'll prototype local lease cache + reconciliation loop this week and post back with perf numbers
Alex C.: perfect — follow up in #eng-runtime next week with results. :thumbsup:
